title: fix(plugin-view): resolve context tokens in the filters ObjectView hands on (objectui#10506)
body:
Fixes #10506
Clause-②: no — a renderer stops sending a spec context token literally; no export, schema or accept set moves.

## What changed

**`@object-ui/plugin-view` — `ObjectView`.** It now sends the spec's context tokens (`{current_user_id}`, `{current_org_id}`) as real values in the authored filters it passes on. It uses the ONE shared `resolveFilterPlaceholders` from `@object-ui/core`, with the session scope the host provides through `useFilterScope()` from `@object-ui/react`. The console shell mounts `FilterScopeProvider` from `useAuth()`'s user and active organization, the same two sources the app-shell `ObjectView` uses for its own `filterScope`. No second resolver and no fallback: a token the scope cannot resolve is left as written, and the resolver warns once, which is the resolver's own rule. The filter is therefore never widened.

- A new hook in `ObjectView.tsx`, `useResolvedFilterSegments`, resolves the three authored filter segments once, in one call: the active view's filter (a named `listViews` entry, else the host `views` entry), `table.filter`, and `table.defaultFilters`.
- An authored filter leaves this component in three places, and all three now read the resolved segments: the non-grid `find()`, the `object-grid` schema handed to `ObjectGrid`, and the `list-view` schema handed to a host's `renderListView`.
- The resolved value is held in state. It is keyed on the raw segments (compared by structure with the package's `isStructurallyEqual`) and on the scope's three members (`currentUserId`, `currentOrgId`, `onUnresolved`), each compared on its own, never the scope object's identity (AGENTS.md #10). The reasons: `ObjectGrid` and `ListView` refetch whenever the filter object's identity changes, and a `{now}` macro gives a new value on every call.

**`@object-ui/core` — the resolver's two object walks (the Date repair).**
- `resolveContextTokens` in `filter-tokens.ts` and `resolveDateMacros` in `date-macros.ts` used to rebuild every object from its own keys. A `Date` has no own keys, so a `Date` comparand came back from `resolveFilterPlaceholders` as `{}`, even though the spec admits `Date` (`ACCEPTED_FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPES`).
- Both walks now descend only into a plain object, whose prototype is `Object.prototype` or `null`. Any other object is a leaf, returned as the same instance: a `Date`, and equally a class instance. A class instance with own keys carrying a token is therefore no longer copied and resolved. The contract review of this change found no in-repo caller that passes one.
- This is two mechanical hunks. There is no new export and no other change to core.
- The defect predates this card. The resolver's existing call sites (app-shell `ObjectView`, `ObjectDataPage`, `useOpenRecordList`; plugin-charts `ObjectChart`; the plugin-dashboard widgets) all get the repair. The plugin-view change above would otherwise have been a tenth door onto it.

**Changeset:** `.changeset/10506-named-view-context-tokens.md`, with `'@object-ui/plugin-view': patch` and `'@object-ui/core': patch`.

**Prose this change would make false, or that AGENTS.md #2 requires:**
- `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`: its sentence saying resolution on the `object-view` node was still tracked in this card is corrected.
- `packages/plugin-view/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`: each gains one paragraph beside the filter-tier precedence.

**Commits:**
- `2218bbbbb` fix(plugin-view): resolve the tokens.
- `fa4f23b3f` docs and changeset.
- `ec06abc38` test typing.
- `bf6a8fbe9` hold in state, not a ref.
- `f0173ec3f` fix(core): non-plain objects are leaves.
- `57eda69be` docs: changeset and docs prose made true to the contract review; prose only.
- `53aa3660c` docs: the ObjectStack auth (401 at the REST auth gate) and timezone (tenant `localization.timezone`) facts corrected; prose only.

## Measured

The code was measured at `f0173ec3f`, base `9cbe4dbca`. `57eda69be` and `53aa3660c` change only the changeset and the three docs files: `git diff --stat f0173ec3f..53aa3660c` lists exactly those four.

- **plugin-view pin** `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.namedViewContextTokens-10506.test.tsx`, 14 cells.
  - Base code: 12 of the first 13 cells fail, each reading the literal `{current_user_id}` where `usr_42` was expected.
  - The Date cell fails at `bf6a8fbe9` (`expected {} to be an instance of Date`).
  - Head: all 14 pass.
- **core pin** `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/filter-tokens.dateLeaf-10506.test.ts`, 5 cells.
  - At `bf6a8fbe9`, the 3 Date cells fail (`expected {} to be 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`). The 2 controls pass: a plain object and a null-prototype object carrying a token are still resolved.
  - Head: 5 of 5 pass.
- **Per-hunk ablation** (`ablation-replace.mjs --delete` of the guard line, each file on its own): `4 failed | 15 passed` for each, with the controls green. Both files were restored: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Earlier checks on the plugin-view hunk:**
  - With the pre-change `ObjectView.tsx` put back: `12 failed | 1 passed`.
  - With the hold changed to resolve on every render: `4 failed | 9 passed`.
- **Suites at `f0173ec3f`:**
  - `packages/core/`: `172 passed`, `3491 passed`.
  - `packages/plugin-view/`: `49 passed`, `477 passed`.
  - The resolver's call-site suites: `73 passed`, `677 passed`.
  - app-shell `views/ObjectView.*` and Studio: `85 passed`, `622 passed`.
  - core and plugin-view type-check: exit 0.
- **Gates at `53aa3660c`, each exit 0:** `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `docs:check-links` and `check:doc-fences`.
  - `check-changeset-claims` is report-only. The 18 listed paragraphs are unchanged in meaning by this prose, and this changeset negates neither package it declares.
- **CI at `f0173ec3f`:** 43 check runs, 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure.

## Acceptance notes

- **Date macros** (`{today}`, `{current_quarter_start}`, …) are now resolved on the client for this node, in the browser's local time.
  - That is the same call the app-shell host, the dashboards and `ObjectChart` already make; a directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node still does not make it.
  - Before, on this node's paths, the macros reached the server as literals. The ObjectStack server resolved them in the tenant's configured `localization.timezone`, UTC by default: REST reads it through `resolveLocalizationContext` into the execution context, and objectql's `resolveWhereTokens` hands that context to `resolveFilterTokens`. So a browser whose local day differs from the server's day can now get a different day.
  - `{now}` and `{today}` are resolved once and held until the user, the organization or a segment changes. A `refreshKey` re-query reuses the held value. This governs the non-grid `find()`, the grid, and any `renderListView` host that queries with the filter it is handed.
  - The console's app-shell host is not one of those: its `renderListView` resolves the active view's own filter itself (`viewDef.filter ?? listSchema.filter`, and the schema it gives this component carries no filter segment). So on the console's delegated grid path the date macros are still resolved by the app-shell on each of its renders, as before. The active view's filter still reaches this component there, through the `views` prop, so this component's pass still runs on it.
- **Context tokens against the backend:** the ObjectStack server also expands `{current_user_id}` for a signed-in request, and refuses the request otherwise: the REST face answers 401 at its auth gate before the filter is read, and where a guest context reaches the engine the resolver answers 400. So against that backend, the literal token this node used to send was expanded, or the request was refused, before the database saw it. This is a source reading, not an end-to-end measurement. The gap this PR closes is on the client, and it still matters for any backend that has no such resolver, where a literal token matches no record.
- **With no user in scope on the console,** only this component's pass warns. The app-shell's own pass substitutes `'current-user'` (`FALLBACK_USER`) silently, as before, so the console's query is unchanged from base and the only difference is one new warning. A host that resolves the handed value again changes nothing: a resolved id or date no longer matches the whole-token pattern (pinned).
- **All three segments are resolved** even when one wins, so a token in a losing segment can warn for a filter that is never sent.
- **Seen from source only, not measured:** a directly authored `object-grid` or `list-view` node still sends its own `schema.filter` tokens unresolved (`plugin-grid` and `plugin-list` have zero reads of the resolver). The contract review calls this a real defect of the same class. The seat filed it as objectui#10607; it is not fixed in this PR.
